title: Gold slips as higher oil, US inflation data bolster Fed hike bets - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Gold prices slipped ⁠on Friday as higher oil prices and robust US inflation data strengthened the case for another Federal Reserve interest rate hike later ‌this year. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto

Gold prices slipped ⁠on Friday as higher oil prices and robust US inflation data strengthened the case for another Federal Reserve interest rate hike later ‌this year.

Spot gold was down 0.9 per cent at $3,982.85 per ounce by 0740 GMT, while US gold futures ‌for December delivery dropped 1 per cent to $3,992.50. Bullion was headed ‌for ⁠a weekly fall and a second consecutive monthly ⁠decline.

"Gold's slide is asking serious questions of technical support around the $4,000 level. Dip buying has previously limited declines, but it remains to be ​seen whether value buying will ‌come to gold's rescue," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.

"There were enough bullish indicators in the US macro data this week to keep the ‌Fed on track for a potential December hike, ​which combined with oil at present levels means that gold continues to lose out from ⁠an inflation perspective."

US inflation accelerated in September as consumers paid more for gasoline and other goods, supporting economists' expectations of ‌an interest rate increase in December.

Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, making gold less attractive to investors.

Traders are pricing in about a 72 per cent chance of a rate hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.

Oil prices rose on Friday ‌and were set for a fourth monthly gain, as an attack on ​a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz highlighted supply risks stemming from the US-Israeli war ⁠on Iran.

Elsewhere, annual core inflation in Japan's capital well exceeded the central ⁠bank's 2 per cent target in October, data showed on Friday, highlighting mounting price pressure.

Spot silver slid 3.1 per cent ‌to $50.74, platinum dropped 3.3 per cent to $1,439.05 and palladium fell 2.3 per cent to $982.50. All three metals were headed for weekly ​and monthly declines.
